en: to seize; to attach; to place under attachment

examples.en: The court seized that person's house.
The tax office seizes the bank account.

examples.ko: 빚을 못 갚으면 월급도 압류할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you can't repay the debt, they can even seize your salary.

examples.ko: 은행이 차를 압류해서 운전을 못 해요.
examples.en: The bank seized the car, so I can't drive.

examples.ko: 재산을 압류하는 일은 아무나 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Not just anyone can seize property.

examples.ko: 세금을 안 내면 재산을 압류한다고 했어요.
examples.en: They said they would seize your property if you don't pay taxes.

explain: 압류하다는 법원, 세무서, 은행 같은 기관이 하는 일이라 개인이 주어면 어색해요. 개인이 남의 물건을 가져가는 건 '뺏다'나 '가져가다'라고 해요. 당하는 쪽은 '압류당하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I had my car seized because I didn't pay taxes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 재산을 묶을 때, 당하는 사람 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used from the view of the person whose property is taken by an authority.

phrases.en: My bank account was seized, so I can't use the money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 주어일 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the passive form, used when the thing seized is the subject.

phrases.en: The court can seize property.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 가진 권리나 가능성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used to talk about what an authority is allowed to do.

explain_en: Legally seizing property over debt, by court or bank. 압류하다 is done by institutions such as a court, tax office, or bank, so it sounds odd with a private person as the subject. When an individual takes someone's things, 뺏다 or 가져가다 is used. The person it happens to is described with 압류당하다.

t90.ax: Not just anyone can seize property.

examples.en: When the contract ends, you have to restore the house to its original state.

examples.ko: 벽에 낸 구멍은 원상회복 비용을 내야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay restoration costs for the holes in the wall.
It was damaged so badly that restoring it is impossible.
The court ordered the company to restore things to their original state.

examples.ko: 공사 후에 길을 원상회복하는 데 일주일이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a week to restore the road after the construction.

examples.ko: 청소뿐 아니라 원상회복까지 끝내고 열쇠를 돌려줬어요.
examples.en: I finished not just the cleaning but the restoration too, and returned the key.

explain: 집을 빌렸다가 나갈 때, 공사를 한 뒤에 쓰는 말로, 바꾼 것을 원래대로 돌려놓는 것을 말해요. '복구'는 망가진 것을 고치는 것 전반에 쓰고, 원상회복은 '원래 상태'로 돌려놓는다는 점을 강조해요. 뉴스나 계약 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I restored the wall to its original state when I moved out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사에 '하다'를 붙인 동사로, 직접 원래대로 돌려놓았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, used when you actually restore something to how it was.
phrases.en_equiv: to restore to the original state

phrases.example: 원상회복 비용은 집주인과 먼저 이야기해야 해요.
phrases.en: You should first talk with the landlord about the restoration cost.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 빌렸다가 나갈 때 돈 문제를 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in money talk when moving out of a rental.

phrases.en: Please put the repaired spot back as it was before you leave.
phrases.nuance_ko: '원상회복'보다 쉬운 일상 표현이라서 말할 때 편하게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say the same thing in conversation.
phrases.en_equiv: to put back as it was

explain_en: It is used when moving out of a rental or after construction work, meaning to put altered things back as they were. '복구' covers repairing damage in general, while 원상회복 stresses returning to the original state. It shows up often in the news and in contract talk.

en: to go against; to be contrary to

examples.en: This action goes against the company rules.

examples.ko: 법에 위배되는 일은 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not do anything that violates the law.
The decision went against the promise, so I protested.

examples.ko: 계약 내용에 위배될 경우 벌금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: If it goes against the contract terms, a fine must be paid.
A ruling came out saying it violates the constitution.

examples.ko: 학교 규정에 위배되지 않는 선에서 해 보세요.
examples.en: Try it within limits that do not go against school regulations.

explain: '어기다'는 사람이 규칙을 직접 어기는 행동이고, '위배되다'는 행동, 결정, 내용이 법, 규칙, 약속에 맞지 않을 때 써요. 그래서 주어는 사람보다 일이나 결정이고, 조사 '에'와 함께 '규칙에 위배되다'로 써요. 계약과 법 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That decision goes against our promise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙뿐 아니라 약속에도 쓸 수 있고, 주어는 결정이나 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for promises as well as rules; the subject is a decision or matter.

phrases.en: This method doesn't go against the rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 없다는 것을 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says there is no problem.

phrases.en: You must not break a promise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위배되다'보다 쉽고, 사람이 직접 어기는 행동에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 위배되다; used for a person directly breaking something.

explain_en: '어기다' is when a person breaks a rule directly. '위배되다' is used when an action, decision or content does not match a law, rule or promise, so the subject is usually a matter or decision rather than a person. It takes '에', as in '규칙에 위배되다', and appears often in contract and legal talk.

examples.ko: 허락 없이 사진을 파는 것은 위법적인 행동이에요.
examples.en: Selling photos without permission is an unlawful act.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 위법적인 관행이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: That company's unlawful practices appeared in the news.
The lawyer argued that this measure is unlawful.

examples.ko: 위법적으로 땅을 사용한 것이 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: Using the land unlawfully became a problem.

examples.ko: 이 계약은 위법적일 가능성이 있어서 다시 검토해야 해요.
examples.en: This contract may be unlawful, so we need to review it again.

examples.ko: 위법적이지 않은지 법률 전문가에게 먼저 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I first asked a legal expert whether it was unlawful.

explain: '불법적'과 비슷하지만 '위법적'은 법규에 어긋났는지 따지는 뉴스나 재판 이야기에 잘 어울려요. 반대말은 '합법적'이에요. '위법적인 N', '위법적이다'로 써요.

phrases.example: 몰래 녹음해서 파는 것은 위법적인 행위예요.
phrases.en: Secretly recording and selling it is an illegal act.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법에 어긋나는 행동을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for an act that breaks the law.

phrases.example: 이 계약 내용은 위법적일 수 있어요.
phrases.en: The terms of this contract may be unlawful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 써서 법에 어긋나는지 판단할 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a predicate when judging whether something breaks the law.

phrases.en: Money earned unlawfully must be returned.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 행동이 어떤 방식으로 이루어졌는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, describing how something was done.

explain_en: It is similar to '불법적', but '위법적' fits news and court talk where people judge whether something breaks a law or regulation. The opposite is '합법적'. It is used as '위법적인 N' or '위법적이다'.

examples.en: My grandfather wrote a will before he passed away.
The lawyer read the will in front of the family.

examples.ko: 유언장에는 재산을 나누는 방법이 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The will described how to divide the property.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 가짜 유언장이 나와서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A fake will appeared in the drama, and I was shocked.
A will must be legally valid.

examples.ko: 그는 서랍 깊숙이 유언장을 숨겨 두었어요.
examples.en: He hid the will deep in a drawer.

explain: 말로 남기면 '유언', 글로 쓴 문서는 '유언장'이에요. '유언장을 쓰다', '유언장을 작성하다', '유언장을 공개하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스와 드라마에 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My father left a will for the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 죽기 전에 문서를 준비해 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preparing a document before one's death.

phrases.en: The contents of the will were in the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유산이나 가족 이야기를 전할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in stories about inheritance and family.

phrases.en: I remember my grandmother's last words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이 아니라 말로 남기는 마지막 부탁이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The final request spoken, not written.

explain_en: A spoken wish is 유언, and the written document is 유언장. You say 유언장을 쓰다, 유언장을 작성하다, 유언장을 공개하다. It appears more in news and dramas than in daily conversation.

t90.ax: A will must be legally valid.

examples.en: The constitution protects citizens' property rights.
The landowner claims to hold the property rights.

examples.ko: 아파트 재건축은 주민의 재산권과 관련이 있어요.
examples.en: Apartment reconstruction is related to residents' property rights.
People gathered to protest, calling it an infringement of property rights.
Individual property rights are guaranteed by law.
I consulted a lawyer about the property rights to the land.

explain: 주로 '재산권을 보호하다', '재산권을 침해하다'처럼 법이나 뉴스 이야기에서 나와요. 특허나 저작권 같은 것은 '지식재산권'이라고 따로 불러요.

phrases.example: 이 법은 시민의 재산권을 침해한다는 비판을 받아요.
phrases.en: This law is criticized for violating citizens' property rights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 권리를 해칠 때 쓰는 말로 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for harming someone's rights; common in the news.

phrases.en: The homeowner exercised his property rights and sold the house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가진 권리를 실제로 사용한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means actually using the right one holds.

phrases.example: 헌법에는 재산권 보장에 대한 내용이 있어요.
phrases.en: The constitution has content about guaranteeing property rights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법이나 제도가 권리를 지켜 준다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a law or system guarantees the right.

explain_en: Legal right to own and use property; law, formal. It mostly appears in talk about law and the news, as in '재산권을 보호하다' or '재산권을 침해하다'. Things like patents and copyrights are separately called '지식재산권' (intellectual property rights).

examples.en: This term is defined by law.
Happiness is defined differently by each person.
Once the problem is defined exactly, it's easier to solve.

examples.ko: 처음에 정의된 뜻과 지금 쓰임이 달라요.
examples.en: The originally defined meaning differs from how it's used now.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 사전에서 어떻게 정의되는지 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I looked up how this word is defined in the dictionary.
The roles aren't clearly defined, so it's confusing.

explain: 단어, 용어, 문제의 뜻이나 범위가 분명하게 정해질 때 써요. 사람이 하는 '정의하다'와 짝이고 '~로 정의되다'로 어떻게 정해졌는지 말해요. 같은 소리의 '정의'(옳은 것, justice)는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: Only the defined terms appear on the test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: Success is defined differently by each person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻을 정하는 방식이 다를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the way of defining something differs.

phrases.example: 이 말의 뜻은 아직 정의되지 않았어요.
phrases.en: The meaning of this word hasn't been defined yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 분명하게 정해지지 않았다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning the meaning has not been clearly set.

explain_en: Used when the meaning or scope of a word, term, or problem is clearly set. It pairs with 정의하다, and you say how with ~로 정의되다. The same-sounding 정의 meaning justice is a different word.

examples.en: The school club decided to expel a member.
The party expelled that lawmaker.

examples.ko: 단체가 규칙을 어긴 사람을 제명할 수 있어요.
examples.en: An organization can expel someone who broke the rules.
The members proposed expelling the president by vote.
Why are you trying to expel me from the group?

examples.ko: 협회는 부정을 저지른 선수를 제명하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The association did not expel the player who cheated.

explain: 'N을/를 제명하다'처럼 단체가 사람을 명단에서 빼 내보낼 때 써요. 일상에서 친구끼리는 '쫓아내다'라고 가볍게 말하기도 하지만, 제명하다는 공식적인 결정이라는 느낌이에요. 반대로 받아 주는 건 '가입시키다'예요.

phrases.example: 그 회원은 규칙을 어겨서 협회에서 제명됐어요.
phrases.en: That member was expelled from the association for breaking the rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제명하다'의 피동형으로, 내보내진 사람을 주어로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive of 제명하다, with the expelled person as the subject.

phrases.en: We expel people who break the rules from the group.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디에서 내보내는지를 '에서'로 함께 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A usage that states what the person is removed from, using '에서'.

phrases.en: I kicked the noisy customer out of the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 결정이 아니라 가볍고 직접적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, direct word, not an official decision.

explain_en: Used as 'N을/를 제명하다' when a group removes a person from its list and sends them out. Friends might casually say '쫓아내다', but 제명하다 sounds like an official decision. The opposite is letting someone in, '가입시키다'.

examples.en: The National Assembly enacted a new law.
The city established an Environment Day.
The school will establish a new rule.

examples.ko: 회사가 안전 수칙을 제정한 뒤 사고가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Accidents decreased after the company set safety rules.

examples.ko: 법을 제정하려면 많은 사람의 동의가 필요해요.
examples.en: To enact a law, you need the agreement of many people.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리는 지금 회칙을 제정하는 중이에요.
examples.en: Our club is in the middle of drawing up its bylaws.

explain: 법, 규칙, 기념일처럼 공식적인 것을 새로 만들어 정할 때 써요. '규칙을 만들다'가 일상 말이고, '제정하다'는 문서나 뉴스에 어울려요. 비슷하게 생긴 '개정하다'는 이미 있는 것을 고친다는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: The country enacted a child protection law.
phrases.nuance_ko: '법', '규칙', '기념일'과 가장 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits best with law, rules, and commemorative days.

phrases.example: 이 법은 십 년 전에 제정됐어요.
phrases.en: This law was enacted ten years ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만들어진 시점을 말할 때 피동형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form is used when stating when something was established.

phrases.en: The school set a new rule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '정하다'가 더 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: 정하다 is easier in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It is used when officially creating and fixing something new, such as a law, rule, or commemorative day. '규칙을 만들다' is the everyday phrase, while '제정하다' suits documents and news. The similar-looking '개정하다' differs: it revises something that already exists.

en: to be concluded; to be signed (contract, treaty, deal)

examples.en: A contract was concluded between the two companies.
Once the agreement is signed, trade gets easier.
I'll send you the contract that was signed yesterday.

examples.ko: 조약이 체결되기 전에 회의를 세 번 했어요.
examples.en: They held three meetings before the treaty was concluded.
The contract will be signed next week.

examples.ko: 합의는 했지만 아직 계약이 체결되지 않았어요.
examples.en: We agreed, but the contract hasn't been signed yet.

explain: 계약·협정·조약처럼 문서로 남기는 약속에 써요. 사람이 주어가 아니라 계약이 주어라서 '계약이 체결되다'로 말하고, 하는 쪽을 말할 때는 '계약을 체결하다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '계약하다', '사인하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The two companies concluded a contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 회사가 주어일 때 쓰는 능동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active expression, used when a person or company is the subject.

phrases.en: I'm signing the contract with the landlord tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '체결하다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, this is used more than 체결하다.

phrases.en: Please sign here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류에 이름을 쓰는 행동을 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to talk about signing your name on a document.

explain_en: Passive: a contract or treaty gets formally signed (계약이 체결되다) Used for formal commitments put on paper: contracts, agreements, treaties. The contract is the subject ('계약이 체결되다'); when you name the people acting, use '계약을 체결하다'. In everyday talk Koreans usually say '계약하다' or '사인하다'.

en: right of control; authority to control

examples.ko: 아이의 휴대폰 사용에 대한 통제권은 부모에게 있어요.
examples.en: Parents have control over their child's phone use.

examples.ko: 이 일은 제 통제권 밖이라서 어쩔 수 없어요.
examples.en: This is outside my control, so there's nothing I can do.

examples.ko: 회사가 모든 정보의 통제권을 갖고 있어요.
examples.en: The company holds control over all the information.

examples.ko: 저는 제 삶의 통제권을 되찾고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to take back control of my life.
It's dangerous when a driver loses control of the car.
I don't know who has taken control of the situation.

explain: '통제권을 갖다/잃다/되찾다/넘기다'처럼 동사와 함께 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '내 마음대로 할 수 없는 일이에요'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 회사 대표가 모든 일의 통제권을 갖고 있어요.
phrases.en: The CEO holds control over everything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 마음대로 할 수 있는 힘이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone has the power to decide things.

phrases.en: The driver lost control of the car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황을 더는 다룰 수 없게 됐을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can no longer handle the situation.

phrases.en: He took back control of the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잃었던 힘을 다시 가질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when regaining power that was lost.

explain_en: Legal or formal right to control something (통제권을 갖다). It is often paired with verbs like '갖다', '잃다', '되찾다' and '넘기다'. In casual talk people often rephrase it, for example '내 마음대로 할 수 없는 일이에요' (It's not something I can decide).

en: to be destroyed; to be shredded; to be annulled

examples.en: The contract was suddenly annulled and everyone was shocked.
When a promise is broken, people lose trust in each other.

examples.ko: 파기된 계약서는 다시 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: A contract that has been annulled can't be used again.

examples.ko: 합의가 파기될 때는 이유를 분명히 알려야 해요.
examples.en: When an agreement is broken off, you must state the reason clearly.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 협약이 파기되어서 거래가 끊겼어요.
examples.en: The two companies' agreement was annulled, so their dealings stopped.
A rumor spread that the engagement had been called off.

explain: 계약, 약속, 조약처럼 서로 지키기로 한 것이 깨질 때 써요. '취소되다'는 행사나 예약처럼 가볍게 없어질 때 써요. 하는 쪽은 '파기하다'이고, 비밀 서류를 없앨 때도 '파기하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The company unilaterally broke the contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: '파기되다'의 능동형으로, 계약을 깨는 쪽을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form of '파기되다', used when the subject is the one who breaks the contract.

phrases.en: Secret documents must be destroyed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 일부러 없앨 때도 '파기하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '파기하다' is also used for deliberately destroying documents.

phrases.en: That treaty has not been cancelled yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 약속이 아직 유지된다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the agreement still stands.

explain_en: Documents discarded or contracts cancelled; official, passive. Use it when something both sides agreed to keep, such as a contract, promise or treaty, gets broken. 취소되다 is for lighter things like events or reservations being cancelled. The active form is 파기하다, which is also used for destroying secret documents.

t90.ax: A contract that has been annulled can't be used again.

en: to destroy; to shred; to annul

examples.ko: 계약을 파기하면 돈을 물어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: If you cancel the contract, you have to pay damages.
Please destroy the documents that aren't important.
The company decided to delete the personal data.
My friend got very angry because I broke our promise.
The court overturned the earlier ruling.
We destroyed the old records according to the rules.

explain: 일상에서는 '약속을 깨다'라고 하고, '계약을 파기하다'는 공식적인 말투예요. 개인 정보나 서류를 완전히 없앨 때도 써요. 법원에서는 앞선 판결을 취소할 때 써요.

phrases.en: He broke the promise and didn't show up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '파기하다'의 일상 표현이에요. 친구 사이 약속에는 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday expression for '파기하다', natural for promises among friends.

phrases.en: The company destroyed the old documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 정보를 완전히 없앨 때 쓰는 공식적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for completely getting rid of documents or information.

phrases.en: The agreement was suddenly annulled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계약이나 합의가 주어일 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form used when a contract or agreement is the subject.

explain_en: You discard documents or cancel a contract; official, active. In daily talk you say '약속을 깨다' (break a promise); '계약을 파기하다' (cancel a contract) is the formal version. It is also used for fully destroying personal data or documents, and for a court overturning an earlier ruling.

t90.ax: The court overturned the earlier ruling.

examples.ko: 그 사업의 합법성을 두고 논란이 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: Controversy is growing over the legality of that business.

examples.ko: 계약하기 전에 이 업체의 합법성을 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check this company's legitimacy before signing a contract.
The court recognized the legality of the protest.

examples.ko: 합법성만 따지지 말고 도덕적으로도 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just consider legality, think about it morally too.

examples.ko: 새 서비스의 합법성이 아직 분명하지 않아요.
examples.en: The legality of the new service is still unclear.
I asked a lawyer about the legality of this method.

explain: '합법'은 법에 맞는 것이고 '합법성'은 그 정도나 성질을 말해요. '합법성을 따지다', '합법성을 인정하다', '합법성 논란'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 반대말은 '불법성'이에요.

phrases.en: The court examined the legality of the contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법에 맞는지 자세히 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when closely examining whether something is lawful.

phrases.en: The government recognized the legality of the business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법에 맞는다고 공식적으로 받아들일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when officially accepting that something is lawful.

phrases.en: Foreigners can also work legally.
phrases.nuance_ko: '합법성'보다 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 부사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverbial form used more often in daily life than 합법성.

explain_en: Being allowed by law; formal, legal context. '합법' means being within the law, and '합법성' refers to that quality or degree. It often appears in news as '합법성을 따지다' (question the legality), '합법성을 인정하다' (recognize the legality) or '합법성 논란' (legality controversy). The opposite is '불법성'.

t90.ax: The court recognized the legality of the protest.

en: to be permitted; to be allowed; to be tolerated

examples.en: Photography is allowed here.
Pets aren't allowed in the dorm.
Dictionary use was allowed during the exam.

examples.ko: 허용된 시간 안에 문제를 풀어야 해요.
examples.en: You must solve the problems within the allowed time.

examples.ko: 조금 늦는 건 허용되지만 너무 늦으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Being a little late is tolerated, but not too late.

examples.ko: 이 정도 실수는 허용될 것 같아요.
examples.en: A mistake this small seems acceptable.

explain: 규칙이나 상황이 그렇게 하는 것을 막지 않을 때 써요. '허가되다'가 신청해서 받는 승인이라면, '허용되다'는 이미 정해진 규칙 안에서 가능하다는 느낌이에요. 표지판에는 '금지'의 반대로 '허용'이라고 써요.

phrases.en: Food is not allowed in the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙으로 안 된다는 것을 부드럽게 알릴 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form politely tells people that a rule forbids something.

phrases.en: Feel free to do it within the allowed range.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허용되는'으로 바꿔 어디까지 괜찮은지 선을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier '허용되는' is used to state how far something is permitted.

phrases.en: Smoking is prohibited here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허용되다'의 반대말로, 규칙이 막고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '허용되다', used when a rule forbids something.

explain_en: Allowed within rules or limits, general policy. Used when the rules or situation don't forbid something. Where '허가되다' implies applying and receiving approval, '허용되다' means it is possible within established rules. On signs, it is the opposite of '금지'.

dis.h: allowed or tolerated within the rules
gh: approved by an authority after a request

p.n: 허가 suggests permission must be asked for; 허용 is a general allowance.
